description: The traffic generator's view: offered vs achieved load (open model), per-step latency as customers feel it, response codes, session outcomes and user-visible anomalies.

panels.title: Arrivals: target vs actual
panels.description: Open workload model: sessions arrive on a schedule whether or not the system keeps up. target = the scenario's arrival rate (dashed); actual = sessions really started per second (loadgen_arrivals_total), in total and per persona; dropped = arrivals the generator could not start (session cap reached). If actual < target the test applies less load than the scenario says and under-reports the damage.

panels.title: Active sessions
panels.description: Virtual users in the middle of a session. Little's law: active = arrival rate x time in system — when the site slows down at constant arrivals, active sessions pile up.

panels.title: Dropped arrivals in range
panels.description: Arrivals the generator skipped in the selected range because it hit its concurrency cap.

panels.title: Time in system (Little's law)
panels.description: Average session duration implied by Little's law (L = λW, so W = L / λ): active sessions / sessions started per second. Rising = customers spend longer per session (slow pages, waiting room, retries).

panels.title: Customer vs server latency (p95)
panels.description: p95 of all loadgen steps (client side) vs p95 of gateway /api requests (server side). A step can include several requests and client-side waiting, so the gap is time the server's own metrics never see.

panels.title: Step latency p50
panels.description: p50 of each funnel step as measured by the virtual customer.

panels.title: Step latency p95
panels.description: p95 of each funnel step as measured by the virtual customer.

panels.title: Step latency p99
panels.description: p99 of each funnel step as measured by the virtual customer.

panels.title: Steps (last 1m)
panels.description: Per-step summary: throughput, latency percentiles and the share of non-2xx responses (business 409s included).

targets.expr:
(
  sum by (step) (rate(loadgen_requests_total{step=~"$step", code!~"2.."}[1m]))
  or
  0 * sum by (step) (rate(loadgen_requests_total{step=~"$step"}[1m]))
)
/
sum by (step) (rate(loadgen_requests_total{step=~"$step"}[1m]))

panels.title: Step outcomes
panels.description: Step completions per second by outcome as classified by the generator.

panels.title: Response codes by step
panels.description: Every HTTP response the virtual users received, by step and status code.

panels.title: Non-2xx by step
panels.description: Only the non-2xx responses. 409 QUEUE_REQUIRED during the spike is the waiting room working; 503/504 are customers failing.

panels.title: Sessions by persona and result
panels.description: Finished sessions per minute. Personas: shopper (browses, thinks, buys) and bot (skips browsing, hammers hot SKUs).

panels.title: Shopper conversion
panels.description: Share of shopper sessions that ended in a paid order (1m).

panels.title: Bot share of purchases
panels.description: Share of converted sessions that were bots. High = scalpers are buying the hot stock. Lab: bot-army.

panels.title: Anomalies per minute
panels.description: Things a real customer would complain about: order_missing_after_pay (lab replica-lag), duplicate_charge_seen (lab double-charge), price_changed_at_checkout (lab stale-price).

panels.title: Order missing after pay
panels.description: Customers who hit 'order_missing_after_pay' in the selected range. Lab: replica-lag.

panels.title: Duplicate charge seen
panels.description: Customers who hit 'duplicate_charge_seen' in the selected range. Lab: double-charge.

panels.title: Price changed at checkout
panels.description: Customers who hit 'price_changed_at_checkout' in the selected range. Lab: stale-price.
